text:
mia: Bringing up 'firelily-embed-v1' on staging. Did a quick fp16 vs int8 compare (onnx opset13). Short-query holdout numbers look odd.

mia: quick results (short queries <=20 tokens): recall@1 fp16=0.772, int8_perchannel=0.754, int8_symmetric=0.692. int6 preliminary is all over the place.

sam: whoa int8_symmetric dropping that much at R@1. Is that across full holdout or concentrated?

mia: concentrated on short-tail. Full holdout R@1: fp16=0.813, int8_pc=0.806, int8_sym=0.803 — so the symmetric quant issue is specific to short queries.

hana: can you paste the eval command + seed so I can repro locally?

mia: Sure:

```
redwood-eval \
  --model firelily-embed-v1 \
  --quant int8_symmetric \
  --holdout /data/holdouts/short_queries.json \
  --k 1,5,10 \
  --seed 42 \
  --batch 256
```

jord: My hunch: scale/zero_point interaction for very short sequences is skewing dot-products. Per-channel quant preserves per-dim scale so it often wins for similarity tasks. Also check whether normalization is applied before or after quantization.

sam: +1. Normalization placement is a common gotcha — norm-before-quant vs norm-after-quant can flip nearest-neighbor ordering.

mia: we currently L2-normalize after quant (i.e., quant -> decode -> norm). Switched to norm-before-quant in a quick rerun and int8_symmetric R@1 went 0.692 -> 0.735 (single quick sweep, not exhaustive).

hana: nice. Can you also produce UMAP/kmeans diagnostic plots to see neighbor collapse? Also compute avg cosine for positives vs negatives to confirm margin erosion.

mia: pasted small summary from the diagnostic run:

"fp16 avg_pos_cos: 0.78 | avg_neg_cos: 0.21"
"int8_symmetric avg_pos_cos: 0.61 | avg_neg_cos: 0.18"
"int8_perchannel avg_pos_cos: 0.75 | avg_neg_cos: 0.20"

mia: UMAP showed tighter cluster overlap for int8_symmetric on the short queries — neighbors more mixed.

jord: If norm-before-quant helps, recommendation: default to per-channel int8 + norm-before-quant in the onboard doc and mark symmetric-int8 as risky for short-tail workloads. Also run multilingual holdouts (en/fr/es) to ensure no language-specific regressions.

mia: launching multilingual sweep now with microbatch=64. I'll tag failing anchors in #embed-failures and attach artifacts.

deploy-bot: Staging autoscaler: +2 nodes added to eng-ml-staging (reason: eval sweep high throughput) at 2026-03-23T14:02:05Z

sam: if int6 keeps being noisy, consider mixed approach: keep centroid storage or final projection in fp16 and quantize only pre-projection activations to int6. Might preserve ranking while saving memory.

mia: noted. Also will measure downstream KNN latency/throughput for each quant config and include in the perf table. If we converge on per-channel int8 + norm-before-quant, we should add a short-query-specific test to the onboarding checklist (and an explicit note about normalization order).

sam: agree. Also capture seed and exact tokenizer (vocab version) in the artifacts — small tokenization differences amplify short-query sensitivity.

mia: will upload results + commands + plots in ~2h and summarize back here. cc @ops (deploy-bot) for capacity heads-up. :thumbsup:
